comment: The code-review golden set (ADR 0071, Consequences), re-pointed by ADR 0072's amendment as a regression harness for the obligations in tools/config/review-obligations.json: four of the eight pattern cases below are the goldenCase an obligation cites, and a case's own incident line still names the defect. Each pattern case is a real commit range from this repository's history in which a defect the repo later documented was merged, and the finding a reviewer should have raised about it. `source` and `rule` are case-insensitive patterns because the reviewer phrases a rule in the source's words; `files` lists every path at which the same defect is fairly located. `ruleId` is optional and is the opposite kind of field: a literal drawn from tools/config/review-rules.json, validated against that catalogue rather than compiled as a pattern. It does two things, and neither is a tightening — it is the sole input to the `strict` annotation, which claims the validator's own axis + ruleId + file hash would have matched and so is never true for an expectation that pins nothing, and it is an alternative way to match, so a reviewer that picked exactly this id scores a hit even when its `source` and `rule` wording drifts off the patterns above. Recall is matched over expected and a pattern case passes at or above `minRecall`. A case may instead be clean-diff (issue #933): a known-good merged pull request that carries `expectsNoBlocking: true` and a `why` in place of `expected` and `minRecall`, and passes when the report carries no Blocking finding — measuring false alarms rather than recall, scored as `clean-pass` or `clean-fail`, never as a recall number. Each case, of either shape, carries a `tier` (ADR 0072). A `frontier` case is one the reviewer misses; it is the reason to run the replay and runs weekly when a reviewer input moved, and on the golden-replay Request Label (ADR 0109). A `guard` case is one the reviewer catches reliably; it carries no new information per run and exists to catch a brief or contract edit silently undoing something that works, so it runs in the first week of a month in which a reviewer input moved, and on a labelled pull request only when that pull request changes the brief or the finding contract. Promotion to `guard` takes three consecutive catches cited in `tierEvidence`; demotion takes one miss. Replayed by .github/workflows/review-golden-replay.yml, never on a push (ADR 0109); scored by tools/scripts/review/score-golden-case.mjs; shape and ranges asserted by tools/scripts/check-review-golden-set.mjs. The reviewer is always today's and the standards are always the case head's (ADR 0102 item 2): the question a case asks is whether today's reviewer, reading the tree as it stood, would catch the defect. A document the head does not contain is not a standard the range could have broken, so a lesson from a later document reaches a case only through the harness the pull request supplies — the rule catalogue, the obligation catalogue and the skill. That is why a candidate whose defect no document at its head names is parked with an obligation as its reentry condition rather than added and scored as a miss (ADR 0102, Consequences). The pattern-case set grows by attribution: when a merged defect is traced to the pull request that introduced it, its range and expected finding go here, with the attribution evidence in the incident line. Two cases may share a range, when two attributed fixes name the same pull request for unrelated defects; the second case's incident line says so, because folding a second expectation into a live case moves its recall denominator mid-flight. The clean-diff set grows by the opposite search: a merged pull request no later fix names as root cause, whose own review raised no Blocking finding, with that evidence in the incident line and the reason it was chosen in `why`. A squash-merged pull request uses the squash commit as head and its first parent as base. A pull request merged with a merge commit uses its branch tip — the merge commit's second parent — as head, and the merge base of that branch and main as base, so main's own drift during the pull request is not in the range. A case leaves `cases` for `retired` when it is unwinnable rather than hard — a wired gate already suppresses its defect (ADR 0074) — and for `parked` when it is merely hard: never caught, but with no reason to think it cannot be won. A parked entry keeps its id reserved exactly as a retired one does, and carries `reentryCondition` in place of `reason`: the fact, checkable independently of anyone's opinion, that puts the case back in `cases`.

cases.tierEvidence: promoted 2026-09-12 on three consecutive catches: run 34441162698 (its first catch in any run), run 34591297535, and the dispatched frontier run 34663295486. The rate-limit void in 34351285079 neither extends nor breaks the streak.
cases.head: 194fd43b4927bb0b63fec611f3175eb8f8d12262

expected.why: the setup writes MAIL_USERNAME and MAIL_PASSWORD as undefined to configure no SMTP auth, but a process.env setter coerces its value to a string, so the transport is built with auth: { user: 'undefined', pass: 'undefined' } while the code reads as though it configures none; delete on both keys was meant (#409). This case is deliberately held out from the consequence checks added on 2026-09-07: the defect is entirely inside the hunk and turns on a language semantic, not on what the hunk does to code the diff never touched. When this case was written no documented rule named it, so the honest report was smell-baseline and inferred, which caps at should-fix — hence no severity floor. The review obligations since gave it a name, and `ruleId` pins that one: an env-assignment site is exactly what obligation-env-assignment-runtime-value asks about. The patterns stay as they were, so a reviewer that still files it as a baseline smell is still matched. The question this case asks is only whether the reviewer sees it

cases.title: A Sync Run the User started refreshes the lists only when the two-second poll happened to see it live
cases.incident: issue #753, fixed by PR #902, introduced by PR #745 (commit 674ddfa on the fix branch carries `Introduced in #745`; base is the merge-base of #745's branch and main, head is its branch tip). The one escaped defect in the 2026-09-28 measurement (docs/review/escaped-defect-rate.md): the reviewer saw #745 and passed it with `comment` on three findings about its ADR status and its migration, none about the page refresh #902 fixed.
cases.head: 9568773f0f91d0b53bc19a0e8f205e3bcdae74eb

expected.why: the diff gave the subscription and carousel refresh exactly two paths and a run the User started can take neither: useSyncRun calls onRunComplete only on a wasLive → not-live transition its own two-second poll observed, and YouTubePageClient's post-PUT claim-wait loop gives up on its 30-second deadline by clearing waitingForClaim and doing nothing else. A Sync Run that finished before any poll read it as live therefore left the page showing the subscriptions and carousel it had before, while the PUT's own response — which already said the run had happened — was discarded (#753). Two documents at this head state the contract the defect turns on — ADR 0080 decision 1 and docs/features/youtube-integration.md both call `GET /sync-status` the single source of truth for a run — so the reviewer has something to cite. What neither states is any rule about refreshing the lists when a run completes, which is why no `ruleId` is pinned and no severity floor is set: a reviewer that files this against ADR 0080, against the feature doc, or as a baseline smell is matched either way, and a baseline smell caps at should-fix. The `rule` pattern is deliberately narrower than the words `refresh` and `stale`: ADR 0080's own decision 1 calls the UI's “keep the page open, do not refresh” warning false, and a finding about that at these same two files is not this defect. The question this case asks is only whether the reviewer sees it

cases.title: The vault export E2E spec reads the downloaded file through Download.path(), which resolves only while the browser shares the test's filesystem
cases.incident: issue #796, fixed by PR #888, introduced by PR #77 (commit eacbfd3 on the fix branch carries `Introduced in #77`, and the helper that pull request added records the same origin in a doc comment in apps/myorganizer-e2e/src/e2e/helpers/download.ts). The 2026-09-28 escaped-defect gather classifies this fix `unreviewed`: #77 merged on 2026-04-29, months before the reviewer went live, so no review ever saw the diff. Deliberately the same range as `export-envelope-drops-tasks`, which the set already traces to the same pull request (fixed by #540): the two defects are unrelated — one in the hardened export envelope, one in the export E2E spec — and folding this expectation into that case would move a live measurement's denominator (9 of 17 lifetime, at `minRecall` 1) mid-flight, which costs more than a second session on the same diff.
cases.head: 7fde881c0a2f57d05bfc92a20c9cbb863dd52200

expected.why: the spec this diff adds reads the exported vault with `const downloadPath = await download.path()` and then `fs.readFile(downloadPath)`, which resolves only while the browser and the test share a filesystem; against a remote or containerised browser `path()` hands the test nothing it can read and every export assertion in the file fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the vault. `download.saveAs(<a path the test owns>)` is the portable read, and is what #888 extracted into readDownloadText (#796). No `ruleId` is pinned and no severity floor is set, for the reason `mail-test-setup-assigns-undefined-to-env` gives: no document at this head names the rule, so the honest report cites the smell baseline. The `rule` pattern deliberately excludes the words `download` and `duplicat`: #888 also extracted six repeated download-then-read blocks out of this same file, and a duplication finding there is not this defect

parked.title: Sync Bookmarks and separate Vault Meta convergence arrive without a restore that clears them or a path that pushes a local wrapping
parked.incident: issues #617 and #589, fixed by PRs #620 and #594, introduced by PR #573 (git log --diff-filter=A -- syncBookmarkStorage.ts → f267817; vaultMetaConverge split 0cce8c1; both in #573); a third attributed fix, PR #907 (commit 16b01c3, `Introduced in #573`), names the same pull request for the same shape — the web write path for array-shaped Vault Blob Types wrote a bare array and a delete only filtered the record out, so the Deletion Log was never written by the pages and a merge with a copy still holding the record resurrected it (issues #546 and #768)
parked.head: bf58bc8276656e287b334a9bae8dc3e0b9c2b96c
parked.reentryCondition: Hard, not unwinnable: no gate covers this range (enum:fanout:check passes cleanly at its head, per docs/review/golden-replay-results.md), so ADR 0074 does not apply and retirement would misstate why the reviewer keeps missing it. Docs/review/REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md's Deferred candidates section holds the matching checklist entry — 'New persisted state has an inverse' — back for exactly one reason: its trigger cannot yet be stated precisely enough to fire only on a write path with no inverse, rather than on every write path in the repo. The case returns to `cases`, at the tier its evidence then supports, the day that entry is promoted into tools/config/review-obligations.json with `goldenCase: sync-bookmarks-without-restore-or-meta-push` — i.e. the day the trigger can be stated precisely. Parked 2026-09-11 (issue #722); see docs/adr/0072-a-golden-case-earns-its-replay-frequency.md and docs/review/golden-replay-results.md. Two facts recorded on 2026-09-30 while tracing issue #934's candidates, because both bear on promotion. First, #907 makes this the third fix attributed to #573 and its defect is the same missing inverse the deferred checklist entry describes, so the trigger that returns this case covers it too and no second case on this range is warranted. Second, the range is 122 files and 22,764 insertions, against 62 files and 5,616 insertions for `export-envelope-drops-tasks`, the largest range any replay has finished inside the 80-turn ceiling in .github/actions/code-reviewer/action.yml: check that budget before promoting, or the run records a void, which measures nothing (ADR 0101). Unlike the two candidates parked beside it, this one does not lack its document — docs/adr/0054-a-vault-blob-converges-by-record-and-absence-is-recorded.md is in the tree at `bf58bc8`, three ADRs before the range's own additions.

parked.title: The React Native app's TypeScript program declares dom in lib, so browser globals typecheck in code that runs on Hermes
parked.incident: issues #882 and #740, fixed by PRs #894 and #901, introduced by PR #159 (squash commit f960e96; base is its first parent). Commits 1f6d52b and a725da5 each carry `Introduced in #159`, and the 2026-09-28 escaped-defect gather counts #159 twice among the nine attributed fixes, both classified `unreviewed`: #159 merged on 2026-06-12, before the reviewer went live, so no review ever saw the diff.
parked.head: f960e96a3b8cbbc92d094ba5585abcf233efb7e5
parked.reentryCondition: Hard, not unwinnable, and not covered by a gate: tools/scripts/check-mobile-platform.mjs does not exist at `f960e96`, so ADR 0074 does not apply and retiring it would misstate why it is not replayed. The defect is one line — apps/mobile/tsconfig.json declares `"lib": ["dom", "esnext"]` for a React Native program, so a browser global typechecks in code that runs on Hermes and a `typeof window` guard does not protect native, because React Native sets `global.window = global` — and what the case lacks is the lesson, not the line. No document at that head names it: the head's AGENTS.md carries no React Native section at all, and ADR 0103, which states the rule, postdates the range by three months. Under ADR 0102 item 2 a document the head does not contain is not a standard the range could have broken, and that ADR's Consequences name the resolution: carry the lesson in the harness, which is the pull request's and reaches every case. The case returns to `cases`, at the tier its evidence then supports, the day tools/config/review-obligations.json carries an entry for a mobile TypeScript program admitting a browser library — a tsconfig covering apps/mobile or libs/mobile whose `lib` includes `dom` — with `goldenCase: mobile-native-program-declares-dom`. One fact to check first: the range is 141 files and 14,036 insertions, more than twice the largest range any replay has finished inside the 80-turn ceiling in .github/actions/code-reviewer/action.yml, so a promotion that does not also buy turns records a void rather than a score (ADR 0101). Parked 2026-09-30 (issue #934).

parked.title: A precondition waived in an ADR rather than in the spec is raised as a Blocking finding over and over on the same pull request
parked.incident: PR #852 (branch cursor/841-remove-todos-compat-48e7, issue #841), which removed the todos compatibility layer under ADR 0003's exit record. Read from the pull request's own review data on 2026-10-01: the reviewer ran eleven times, 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-19. Runs 1 to 3 (heads 83f23cf, 5d42b94, 1d4e439) raised the unmet precondition as a Blocking Spec finding before any waiver existed, which was correct. The maintainer recorded the waiver at 09:41 UTC on 2026-09-19, in a comment on issue #841 and in ADR 0003, and runs 4 to 10 (heads 5835210, d869b56, b4c4815, 6f3335b, 1729de4, and b86a529 twice) raised the waived 'prior warning release' precondition as Blocking again, seven runs and seven different titles; run 9 raised a second Blocking finding beside it, that the removal commit predates the commit recording the exit evidence. Run 11 (run 35440434756, head 7e01e9d) returned verdict Comment with no Blocking finding on either axis: its one finding is a should-fix restating the waiver. The branch's own commit messages cite sixteen distinct review finding ids they answer. No later fix names it as root cause: `git log --all --grep="Introduced in #852"` is empty.
parked.head: 7e01e9d0e3e7881ca61dcf376eff4c190c73f980
parked.reentryCondition: Hard, not unwinnable, and of the clean-diff shape rather than the pattern shape (issue #933): what is measured here is the reviewer staying quiet about a waived precondition, so the case would carry `expectsNoBlocking: true` and its pass would be silence. Two conditions kept it parked on 2026-09-30 and both now hold. (1) The clause it measures is in the reviewer's brief: slice #938 put it there, and a grep of .agents/skills/code-review for `waive` finds it in the Spec brief. (2) A clean case is admitted on the evidence that the merged head's own review raised no Blocking finding, and the incident line now names, from the pull request's own review data, what stood at `7e01e9d`: nothing Blocking. What still keeps it out of `cases` is a third fact, found when those two were checked: the waiver is a Spec-axis fact, and every case in this set carries `spec: { kind: none }`, so a replay of this range would hand the reviewer no spec source, the Spec brief's waiver clause would never be reached, and a clean pass would measure nothing about it — the shape ADR 0101 refuses to record as a result. The case enters `cases` as a clean case the day a Golden Case can carry issue #841 as its spec source with the waiver in it; the brief counts only a waiver recorded in the issue itself, and on #841 it is in a comment (issuecomment-5740823613), not in the body, whose acceptance checklist was never updated. Parked 2026-09-30 (issue #934); conditions re-read 2026-10-01.

retired.title: The groceries UI is written against Material Design 3 role names that no token or Tailwind config defines
retired.incident: ADR 0065, issue #632, fixed by PR #636, introduced by PR #108 (git log -S surface-container-low -- libs/web/pages/groceries → 9382c16)
retired.head: c0f1a10b0c81d66175c3d46cecd58b1cb8ba3b64
retired.reason: Unwinnable rather than hard. `tailwind:classes:check` — the gate ADR 0065 added as the fix for this very incident — exits 0 at this case's base and exits 1 at its head, naming the same 25 utilities the expected finding is about. It is a wired gate (invoked by .github/workflows/ci.yml), and per ADR 0074 a wired gate's defect is a suppressedRedundant count and not a finding, so a reviewer that loaded ADR 0065 and ran the gate would have been correct to say nothing. The case scored the reviewer as missing what it is instructed not to report. Retired 2026-09-08; see docs/review/golden-replay-results.md.
